description: Passionate young individuals trying to map Mars!
summary: Martian Map is an interactive web map for a future Mars crew to plan a safe, science-rich Marswalk at Gale Crater. One zoomable view combines NASA optical (Viking, CTX down to 5 m per pixel), topographic (MOLA) and thermal (THEMIS, TES) data. Slope-hazard overlay from MOLA elevation indicates walkable, caution or avoid terrain. Users can click on waypoints to see distance, ascent and descent, steepest slope, the percentage of the route in each hazard class, and an elevation profile color-coded by slope from Bradbury Landing to Mount Sharp. It addresses this by turning regional and global Mars data into a route-level planning tool, with safety information in the same view as the science context.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Martian Map is a browser-based, zoomable map of Mars with a route planner for a human Marswalk at Gale Crater, where the Curiosity rover has been climbing Mount Sharp. A crew member or mission planner can switch between seven NASA layers and fade them over one another:

- Optical: Viking color mosaic and CTX mosaics down to about 5 m per pixel (Gale-specific and global)

- Topographic: MOLA elevation shading

- Thermal: THEMIS day and night infrared, and TES thermal inertia

A slope-hazard overlay for the Gale area colors terrain green (under 10 degrees, walkable), yellow (10 to 20 degrees, caution), or red (over 20 degrees, avoid). The user turns on route planning and clicks waypoints, for example, from Bradbury Landing toward Mount Sharp. The tool immediately reports distance, estimated walking time, total ascent and descent, steepest slope, the percentage of the route in each hazard class, and an elevation profile colored by slope, with a warning if the route crosses steep terrain. Science targets (Bradbury Landing and the highest point of Mount Sharp's central mound, computed from the elevation data) have fly-to buttons, and a hover readout shows position, elevation, and slope under the cursor.

HOW IT WORKS

CesiumJS renders Mars as a sphere (radius 3,396,190 m) and streams map tiles from NASA Mars Trek WMTS services at the right resolution as the user zooms. The global 5 m CTX mosaic comes from an Esri-hosted service. A MOLA 463 m elevation model was cropped to Gale with GDAL (gdal_translate), slope was computed with gdaldem, and the cropped elevation grid is read directly in the browser. The route tool samples elevation every 100 m with bilinear interpolation and computes slope from neighboring cells. We checked the elevation data against NASA's published landing-site elevation: our DEM gives -4500 m at Bradbury Landing versus NASA's -4501 m.

BENEFITS

Existing tools show regional and global views. Martian Map brings optical, topographic, and thermal context and a slope-based safety check into one route-level view, so a crew can judge distance and climb steep ground before leaving the habitat. Thermal layers hint at ground type, since loose dust and bedrock hold heat differently.

LIMITATIONS

The elevation model is 463 m per pixel, so slopes are regional and do not show boulders or small obstacles. The slope classes and the 2.5 km/h walking speed are illustrative assumptions, not NASA mobility limits. Elevation, slope, and route planning cover the Gale area only. Radiation data is not yet included.

WHAT WE HOPE TO ACHIEVE

A foundation for crew-facing planning tools: adding radiation data, boulder-scale hazards from HiRISE, boxwork science targets on Mount Sharp, other landing regions, and tablet or helmet-display versions.

TOOLS

JavaScript, CesiumJS, Vite, HTML/CSS, GDAL (gdal_translate, gdaldem), Git and GitHub, and Vercel for hosting. An early prototype used Three.js.
